props.title: Letters to Juliet
props.initialSlug: An American finds love while playing matchmaker in Italy

sections.content: Letters to Juliet (2010) spearheaded a charming wave of Italian-set romance films that blend travel escapism with love stories. Following Sophie's discovery of unanswered romance letters in Verona, the film taps into the timeless appeal of missed connections and second chances. This theme resonates through similar European-set romances like Under the Tuscan Sun (2003) and Only You (1994), where American women find unexpected love amid picturesque Italian landscapes. The film cleverly uses Shakespeare's most famous romance as a backdrop while crafting its own modern love story.

sections.content: The success of Letters to Juliet sparked renewed interest in romantic travel films, particularly those set in Italy. To Rome with Love (2012) continued this tradition with interconnected love stories in the Eternal City, while The Lizzie McGuire Movie (2003) brought the Italian romance formula to younger audiences. These films share a common DNA: the transformative power of Italian culture, food, and atmosphere on Americans seeking love or meaning.

The film's multigenerational approach to romance distinguishes it from typical romantic comedies. Like The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel (2011) and It's Complicated (2009), it proves love stories aren't just for twenty-somethings. Vanessa Redgrave's character Claire embodies the film's message that it's never too late for love, a theme that would influence later works like Book Club (2018). sections.content: Letters to Juliet belongs to a rich tradition of films where travel catalyzes romance. From classic Roman Holiday (1953) to modern entries like Before Sunrise (1995), these stories use foreign locations to create magical spaces where love feels more possible. The film's Verona setting deliberately evokes Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, but transforms tragic romance into hopeful possibility.
